authority_scope: arcs-srs owns this binding's serialization contract: the registered identity, the outgoing statement profile, the carrier and the disclosure limits. Verification findings, their routing and their output names belong to ARCS Verify and are proposed separately in verifier-handoff.json.

relation_mode.label: transparency_registration
relation_mode.note: Proposed label only. Governing doctrine s10 owns the relation-mode vocabulary; this file does not register the label there.

relation_to_existing_work.this_binding_is: the SRS-specific RFC 9995 construction that the reconciliation note recommends in section 4.2 for a separate owner decision, offered as a machine-backed candidate for that decision
relation_to_existing_work.capture_witness_construction: unchanged, unwired and unrepaired: the capture-specific JSON statement signed downstream is neither an RFC 9995 hash envelope nor an SRS receipt (reconciliation note section 4.1)
relation_to_existing_work.sequencing: the reconciliation note's recommendation to replay the existing capture path first is unaffected; the order is an owner decision

native_authority.title: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains
CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts
CBOR Web Token (CWT) Claims in COSE Headers
CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Structures and Process
CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Header Parameters for Carrying and Referencing X.509 Certificates

subject.digest_input: the complete exact receipt bytes as retained, including the receipt_signature object
subject.reserialized_receipt: a different artifact; it needs its own registration
subject.out_of_scope: objects modeled on SRS that are not SRS receipts. Such an object need not become an SRS receipt to be registered; it can use its own outer construction, as the capture-witness path does. It is simply not a subject of this binding.

identities_not_to_conflate.object: SHA-256 of the complete exact receipt bytes
SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 preimage the SRS signature covers
identities_not_to_conflate.role_here: not used; reserializations of one receipt share it
a local sidecar index; not copied into the statement payload or subject; permitted metadata values require deployment disclosure review

identities_not_to_conflate.object: SHA-256 of the exact Signed Statement bytes as submitted
identities_not_to_conflate.role_here: custody of the submitted statement; part of the proposed evaluation relationship

identities_not_to_conflate.object: SHA-256 of the exact native Receipt bytes as returned
identities_not_to_conflate.role_here: identifies the native proof artifact, not a complete finding set; the proposed handoff also binds the target-artifact and signed-statement digests and evaluation context

identities_not_to_conflate.object: SHA-256 of a Signed Statement with Receipts attached under label 394
identities_not_to_conflate.role_here: not carried; a separate representation whose digest is not the signed statement digest

identities_not_to_conflate.object: the leaf value the selected proof profile commits to
identities_not_to_conflate.role_here: computed by the verifier under that profile; never assumed equal to any digest above

identities_not_to_conflate.object: the capture-binding identifier of the existing capture-witness path
identities_not_to_conflate.role_here: not used by this binding; that path keeps its own identity law

signed_statement.payload: embedded; exactly the 32-byte SHA-256 digest of the exact receipt bytes

protected_header_allowlist.name: alg
protected_header_allowlist.note: RFC 9943 marks alg optional, but the unprotected header is empty, so the protected header is the only place the statement can carry its algorithm

protected_header_allowlist.name: kid
protected_header_allowlist.presence: required unless x5t (34) or x5chain (33) is present (RFC 9943 section 6)

protected_header_allowlist.name: x5chain
protected_header_allowlist.discloses: complete certificate data, which can identify the signing organization or person

claims_allowlist.name: iss
claims_allowlist.rule: identifier of the statement issuer: the party that signed this Signed Statement

claims_allowlist.name: sub
claims_allowlist.rule: MUST equal the RFC 6920 ni URI of the exact-artifact digest: ni:///sha-256;<base64url digest without padding>

protected_header_allowlist.name: payload_preimage_content_type
protected_header_allowlist.presence: required by this binding; optional in RFC 9995

protected_header_allowlist.name: payload_location
protected_header_allowlist.presence: optional; included only where a disclosure decision opts in
protected_header_allowlist.rule: a locator hint; never an identity, and never dereferenced to establish identity

signed_statement.labels_outside_allowlist: not permitted, including crit (2) and private-use labels
signed_statement.unprotected_header_as_submitted: empty map; nothing is carried outside the signature
signed_statement.cbor: well formed; a map with duplicate keys is malformed

statement_issuer.is: the party that signed the Signed Statement, named by CWT iss
is_not: necessarily the SRS receipt's issuer or signing key
the submitting client: RFC 9943 lets a client register a statement on an issuer's behalf, and this binding records no submitter

receipt.per_entry: exactly one native Receipt per sidecar entry, carried as its own bytes beside the Signed Statement it was issued for
receipt.service_identity: taken from the authenticated Receipt and matched against verifier-selected trust material; never from the sidecar's service hints
receipt.receipt_header_requirements: those of RFC 9942 and the selected proof profile; this binding adds none

proof_types_not_relied_on.name: consistency
proof_types_not_relied_on.note: an auditor concern; outside this binding

verifiable_data_structures.name: RFC9162_SHA256
verifiable_data_structures.note: Specified by this candidate. No verifier has replayed a real Receipt of this kind under this binding.

verifiable_data_structures.name: CCF_LEDGER_SHA256
verifiable_data_structures.note: No registry value is assigned yet. A verifier that implements the draft may evaluate such a Receipt and must name the structure and draft it verified against. A CCF result says nothing about the RFC9162_SHA256 path.

receipt.transparent_statement: not carried. A Transparent Statement (the Signed Statement with Receipts attached under label 394, RFC 9943 section 7) can be assembled from an entry when a tool needs one; it is a separate representation.

carrier.carries: completed evidence only: for each registration, the exact submitted Signed Statement and the exact returned Receipt
carrier.not_carried: pending, timed-out or refused submissions and transport responses. They are not registrations, and their absence from a sidecar proves nothing about the remote outcome.
carrier.byte_checks_first: base64url decoding and digest equality are checked before any content is read; an entry that fails them is not evaluated
carrier.duplicates: exact duplicate entries are rejected by the schema. Repeated Receipt bytes add no independent source, but do not make different statement/artifact relationships equivalent. The proposed handoff deduplicates complete findings only for the same three digests and evaluation context; no failed pairing may be suppressed.
carrier.separate_attempts: registrations of one statement on one service produce different Receipts and stay separate entries

hints.status: unauthenticated carrier hints; never a basis for a finding. A disagreement with authenticated evidence is reported, never resolved in the hint's favour.

carrier.authenticated_evidence_rule: a value counts only where a verified signature covers it; a value merely carried inside a COSE object, for example in an unprotected header, is not authenticated

registration_interface.rule: any interface the Transparency Service offers; this binding depends on none

registration_time.native_definition: RFC 9943 section 7: the timestamp recorded when the Transparency Service added the Signed Statement to its Verifiable Data Structure
registration_time.authenticated_means: covered by the Receipt's verified signature, defined as a registration time by the selected proof profile, and accepted by the verifier's selected time policy
registration_time.receipt_profile_dependency: this binding assumes no Receipt carries an authenticated registration time, and relies on one only where the selected proof profile defines it
registration_time.meaning_when_authenticated: the exact receipt bytes existed no later than that time, under three assumptions: the Transparency Service's trust, the accepted time policy, and SHA-256 preimage resistance
registration_time.service_custody: This registration construction does not transmit the original receipt bytes. Its proof establishes no custody of those bytes by the transparency service and does not prove the service never obtained them elsewhere.
registration_time.unauthenticated_values: a time in an unprotected header or in the sidecar is reported as an unauthenticated observation and never supports a time bound
registration_time.ordering_note: Verifiable Data Structure order need not match issuance order unless the Registration Policy says so (RFC 9943 section 9.1)

disclosure.constrained_by_this_binding: the Signed Statement: its payload is the digest, its protected header is limited to the allowlist, and its unprotected header is empty
disclosed_by_a_conforming_statement: the SHA-256 digest of the exact receipt bytes, as payload and as sub
the key reference: kid (an opaque identifier), x5t (a thumbprint) or x5chain (complete certificate data)
payload_location, only where a disclosure decision opts in
not_constrained_by_this_binding: the submission interface's metadata: client authentication, network addresses, request headers and timing
the Transparency Service's own records, logs and Registration Policy
disclosure.correlation: the digest is a stable handle for these exact bytes across services and over time
disclosure.retention_labels: a receipt's own retention label, such as hash_only under the MCP SDK enforcement profile (section 3.1), neither authorizes registration nor establishes confidentiality
disclosure.public_service_effect: registration on a public Transparency Service publishes the disclosed values; a transparency log is append-only by design, so treat a registration as permanent
disclosure.authorization_note: Conformance to this binding never authorizes a submission, a disclosure, a choice of service, a retry on another service, or the use of a key. Each of those is a decision for whoever governs the deployment.
disclosure.permitted_metadata: Permitted metadata values (including payload_location, iss, kid and certificate data) remain disclosure-sensitive and can contain receipt identifiers or other sensitive content. They must satisfy the deployment's explicit approval and prohibited-content rules; the deployment governs that review. Header-label allowlists do not enforce value-level nondisclosure.
disclosure.structural_profile_pass: A structural profile PASS is not a nondisclosure finding and does not authorize disclosure or submission.

limitation_codes.description: Registration shows that a named statement issuer signed a commitment to these exact receipt bytes and that a named Transparency Service's proof includes that statement. It does not identify who submitted it.
limitation_codes.renders_as: Registration shows only that a named issuer signed a commitment to this receipt's exact bytes and that a named transparency service's proof includes it.

limitation_codes.description: Registration does not establish that the attested event occurred, that the receipt's contents are true, or any admission, standing or publication state
limitation_codes.renders_as: Registration does not establish that the recorded event happened or that the receipt is true.

limitation_codes.description: A registration time is the Transparency Service's assertion of when it recorded a commitment to this receipt's digest. It is not issued_at, it is not independently witnessed, and it supports a time bound only when authenticated.
limitation_codes.renders_as: A registration time is the transparency service's record of when it logged a commitment to this receipt, not when the receipt was issued.

limitation_codes.description: A receipt without a registration is not invalid; registration is additive
limitation_codes.renders_as: An unregistered receipt is not invalid for that reason.

limitation_codes_note: Binding-local. These are candidate additions to schemas/limitation-codes/v0.1, deferred because that file is pinned by the C2PA binding's semantic digest.
forbidden_inferences: registration implies a valid SRS receipt signature
an unauthenticated time value supports a time bound
the Transparency Service held the receipt bytes
iss identifies who submitted the statement
a transport success response implies registration
absence of a sidecar entry implies the receipt was never registered
a single transparency service is authoritative
several registrations are independent sources, a quorum, or global consistency
conformance to this binding authorizes submission or disclosure
the Transparency Service never obtained the receipt bytes elsewhere

presentation.registration_verified_label: A consumer that shows one 'registration verified' label must define it as the subject binding, statement profile, statement signature, receipt inclusion, statement issuer trust and Transparency Service trust findings all passing under named trust input, and must show the SRS receipt's own findings, time evidence and log consistency separately.

srs_receipt_for_registration_events.reason: A Receipt is verifiable offline (RFC 9943 section 4). An SRS receipt asserting a registration would be a weaker, emitter-asserted copy of a stronger native artifact.
